reconcile.note: Henry places Cain's reprieve and the Genesis 9:6 death penalty in different eras, with judgment reserved to God before the Flood and delegated to human courts afterward.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible juxtaposes God's protection of Cain from execution with the blanket demand in Genesis 9:6 that a murderer's blood be shed.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Does God approve of capital punishment?"

sides.snippet: Therefore whoever slays Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.
sides.verseText: Yahweh said to him, \"Therefore whoever slays Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.\" Yahweh appointed a sign for Cain, lest any finding him should strike him.

sides.snippet: Whoever sheds man's blood, by man will his blood be shed, for in the image of God made he man.
sides.verseText: Whoever sheds man's blood, by man will his blood be shed, for in the image of God made he man.
